# Which four-bit permutations mix?

Let D be the 15 nonzero XOR differences. Each round applies the same P after a
fresh uniform XOR key. We ask whether, from every starting difference, the
distribution converges to uniform on D. This is equivalent to pairwise mixing
of the cipher. The extra cipher round needed to convert a difference distance
to an ordered-pair distance has no effect on whether convergence occurs.

| Outcome | Labeled permutations |
|---|---:|
| Mixes | 20,873,902,694,400 |
| Disconnected | 48,887,150,592 |
| Connected, period 15 | 43,008 |
| Total | 20,922,789,888,000 |

The exact mixing fraction is **179,759/180,180**. The failure fraction is
**421/180,180**. Two descriptions give the same counts. The structural test
recognizes individual failures and the graph enumeration establishes that these
families exhaust the possibilities.

## A test on the 16 images

1. If P is affine, P(x) = Ax ⊕ c, the difference after one round is always Aa.
   The difference walks around one cycle deterministically. A single 15-cycle
   gives the connected periodic cases. Several cycles give disconnection.
2. Check each of the 15 lines, 35 planes and 15 hyperplanes W of F₂⁴. The cosets
   of W are preserved as a partition exactly when
   P(x ⊕ w) ⊕ P(x) belongs to W for every x and w in W. This traps every
   nonzero starting difference in W inside W forever. P may permute the cosets.
3. Every remaining four-bit permutation mixes. The same criterion holds at five
   bits, and a six-bit counterexample shows its limit. [Proofs for larger dimensions](LARGER_BITS.md)

`find_obstruction(P)` returns a subspace witness, an affine order, or `None`
for a mixing permutation. [Implementation](four_bit_obstructions.py)

## Why the fraction changes

For a fixed nonzero parity h, write H for the inputs where h·x = 0. Its image
under a random permutation of N points is a uniform subset of size N/2.
Precisely two images, H and its complement, preserve this parity split.

| | 3 bits | 4 bits |
|---|---:|---:|
| Number of parity splits | 7 | 15 |
| Probability of preserving a specified split | 2/70 = 1/35 | 2/12,870 = 1/6,435 |
| Probability of preserving at least one split, with overlaps removed | 17.936508% | 0.232657% |
| Probability of any failure to mix | 20% | 0.233655% |

Doubling the number of points makes a particular parity obstruction about
184 times rarer. The number of candidate parities only grows from 7 to 15.
These obstructions account for about 99.57% of all four-bit failures.

The convergence curves also gain freedom. Every coordinate of a three-bit
permutation takes the value one four times. Its cubic coefficient, the XOR
of all eight truth-table values, vanishes. Each coordinate therefore has
degree at most two, and its derivative in a fixed direction is affine. Each
transition row is uniform on an affine subspace of size 1, 2 or 4. At four
bits cubic coordinates can occur, and their quadratic derivatives can give
different probabilities to different successors in the same row. All 10,000
permutations in the saved sample had degree three and at least one such row.
This explains a constraint that disappears at four bits. The exact three-bit
curve count also depends on the alignment of successive rows.

## Counting the disjoint failure families

XORing a constant into all outputs preserves differences. Work with P(0) = 0
and restore the 16 possible output translations at the end. The following table
gives full counts and assigns any overlap to the earliest applicable row.

| First obstruction | Permutations |
|---|---:|
| Invariant hyperplane partition | 48,678,419,456 |
| Invariant line partition | 119,116,800 |
| Invariant plane partition | 89,592,832 |
| Irreducible affine linear part of order 5 | 21,504 |
| Irreducible affine linear part of order 15 | 43,008 |

**Hyperplanes.** The masks h satisfying h·P(x) = h·x ⊕ cₕ for every x form a
linear space. Fix k independent masks. Their joint values partition the inputs
into 2ᵏ equal cells. The induced map on the cells is one translation, and the
permutation inside each cell is arbitrary. This gives
2ᵏ ((2ⁿ⁻ᵏ)!)^(2ᵏ) choices of P for a specified k-dimensional mask space.
To remove overlaps, count incidences with all k-dimensional mask spaces,
working down from k = n. A j-dimensional space contributes exactly as many
times as it contains k-dimensional subspaces. The same calculation gives
7,232 parity-preserving permutations at three bits.

**Lines after hyperplanes.** Fix the line generated by the last coordinate.
Write a normalized map preserving its pairs as P(y,z) = (Q(y), z ⊕ f(y)),
with y a three-bit string and f(0) = 0. Q must preserve no parity, leaving
7! − 7,232/8 = 4,136 choices. Of 128 possible f, precisely eight give a
preserved parity involving z. They are f(y) = h·(y ⊕ Q(y)), one for each
h, distinct because Q preserves no parity. This leaves 120 choices.

Two preserved lines would force a preserved hyperplane. In coordinates along
their two directions a normalized P has the form (Q(y), z ⊕ f(y)) with both
y and z two-bit vectors. Q is linear because every normalized two-bit
permutation is linear. A fixed parity of Q is already sufficient. Otherwise
I ⊕ Q is invertible. Choose a nonzero linear bit of the two-coordinate f
that kills its sole possible quadratic coefficient, leaving a linear function
of y. Adding a suitable linear bit of y then makes that bit of z invariant.
Thus the line count is 16 × 15 × 4,136 × 120 with no overlap.

**Planes after hyperplanes and lines.** For a fixed invariant plane, let z be
the two fiber coordinates and y the two quotient coordinates. Every normalized
map has the form (Cy, Mᵧz ⊕ cᵧ). The two choices of C with order three avoid
a fixed quotient parity or line. The three free offsets give 4³ choices.
The four invertible binary matrices Mᵧ must have no common fixed nonzero
vector. This also excludes a common fixed parity because GL(2,2) preserves the
nondegenerate alternating form identifying vectors with linear functionals.
Inclusion-exclusion on three directions gives 6⁴ − 3·2⁴ + 2 = 1,250 matrix
tuples. This yields 160,000 normalized maps per plane.

Two different preserved planes must be complementary here, since their
intersection would otherwise be a preserved line. Preserving their two
partitions separately makes P act linearly on both two-bit coordinates.
Each restriction has order three. Equivalently, the vector space becomes
two-dimensional over F₄ with P acting by multiplication by a root of
x²+x+1. Its five F₄-lines are exactly its invariant binary planes. There
are |GL(4,2)| / |GL(2,4)| = 112 such maps, all conjugate. Removing four extra
counts per map gives 16 × (35 × 160,000 − 4 × 112).

**Remaining affine maps.** A linear map preserving no proper nonzero subspace
is multiplication by an element of degree four over F₂. Its order is 5 or
15. In the cyclic group F₁₆* there are four elements of order 5 and eight
of order 15. Each four conjugate elements specify one irreducible quartic.
The invertible linear maps commuting with any one such multiplication are exactly the
15 nonzero field multiplications. Each quartic therefore contributes
16 × |GL(4,2)| / 15 = 21,504 labeled affine maps.

## How the graph count checks exhaustiveness

The [exact verifier](exact_four_bit.py) labels the edge between x and y of the
complete graph on the 16 input points by the difference x ⊕ y. A partition of
the 15 differences groups these labels into colors. For each partition it
counts the permutations fixing zero that preserve every edge color, using
backtracking and the orbit-stabilizer formula.

Such a permutation has every difference transition inside its current color.
Its actual component partition therefore refines the proposed partition.
Conversely, any union of components is closed. To count a given component
partition exactly, subtract the counts for all its strict refinements.

The search only needs partitions that can arise as the orbits of a color-
preserving group fixing zero. Every component partition has this property.
Each path of difference transitions lifts to a composition of P and point
translations on pairs. A final translation brings the first endpoint back to
zero. Start with one color and repeatedly split a cell and take the group
orbits. When pursuing a target component partition, splitting along a union
of target cells retains its group and cannot refine past the target. Linear
changes of basis reduce the search to **43 types** representing **12,537
labeled partitions** at four bits.

For a connected periodic chain the period divides 15 because the cyclic
classes have equal stationary mass. For each divisor 3, 5 and 15 the verifier
counts the maps rotating equal-size colors by one step and checks connectivity.
These partitions are covered by the same search: a path between states of the
same cyclic color has length zero modulo the number of colors and its lift
preserves the colors. Each connected chain has a unique unordered cyclic
partition for each divisor of its period. Removing the contributions of
larger periods leaves zero cases of exact period 3 or 5 and 43,008 of period
15. For period 15 every cyclic class is a singleton, so the successor of a is
independent of the input x. Taking P(0) = 0 gives
P(x ⊕ a) ⊕ P(x) = P(a) for every x and a, precisely linearity. The component
counts and period counts match the five structural families above.
